title: Topic Detection and Tracking with Time-Aware Document Embeddings
read_from: arXiv preprint 2112.06166 (earlier version; published version: LREC-COLING 2024)
subcategory: topic detection and tracking (event clustering) with time-aware embeddings
task: Retrospective and online clustering of news stories into events
problem: Time metadata is central to topic detection and tracking, but earlier systems do not capture how time interacts with event semantics (short-lived vs long-running events).
architecture: T-E-BERT: entity-aware BERT text encoder fused with a sinusoidal position embedding of the document timestamp (daily granularity) via concatenation + multi-head attention + mean pooling, fine-tuned with batch-hard triplet loss; embeddings clustered with HDBSCAN or group-average agglomerative clustering (retrospective) or plugged into an online TDT pipeline.
key_results: News2013, HDBSCAN: B-Cubed F1 90.04 with SinPE-E-BERT vs 75.79 for E-BERT and 70.48 for TF-IDF.
TDT-1: TF-IDF + HDBSCAN is best (F1 91.16 vs 88.83).
Daily granularity works best on News2013 (F1 90.04 vs 77.20 monthly).
strengths: Simple fusion of time and text that helps with recurring events; ablations on time encoding, fusion and granularity.

limitations.text: Does not beat TF-IDF on the small TDT-1 dataset; English news only.
Event-level clustering rather than probabilistic topic mixtures; time granularity must be tuned per dataset.

notes: Included as event-level topic detection related to dynamic topic modelling.
